sentences.zh: 孝景采《武德儛》以為《昭德》，孝宣又采《昭德》以為《盛德》，雖變其名，大抵皆因秦舊事。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing adapted the "Wude Dance" as "Zhaode"; Emperor Xuan further adapted "Zhaode" as "Shengde"—though the names changed, all largely followed Qin precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing reworked the "Wude Dance" into "Zhaode," and Emperor Xuan reworked "Zhaode" into "Shengde"—the titles changed, but all essentially followed Qin precedent.

sentences.zh: 至於魏、晉，皆用古樂。

translations.literal: As for Wei and Jin, both used ancient music.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin alike, the court still employed the ancient music.

sentences.zh: 魏之三祖，並制樂辭。

translations.literal: The three founders of Wei all composed texts for music.
translations.idiomatic: The three founding emperors of Wei all composed lyrics for court music.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，五都傾蕩，樂聲南度，是以大備江東。

translations.literal: From the upheaval of Yongjia, when the five capitals were overturned, musical sounds crossed south—hence the eastern lands were richly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia upheaval overturned the five capitals, musical traditions fled south—and so the lands east of the Yangtze came to preserve them in full.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊已來，至於梁代，所行樂事，猶皆傳古，三雍四始，實稱大盛。

translations.literal: From Song and Qi through the Liang dynasty, the musical ceremonies practiced still transmitted the ancient tradition; the Three Yong and Four Beginnings truly marked a great flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: From Song and Qi through the Liang, the music performed at court still transmitted the ancient rites—the Three Yong and Four Beginnings marked a true golden age.

sentences.zh: 及侯景篡逆，樂師分散，其四儛、三調，悉度偽齊。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing usurped power, music masters scattered; the four dances and three modes all passed to the puppet Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, court musicians scattered, and the four dances and three modes all passed into the hands of the puppet Qi regime.

sentences.zh: 齊氏雖知傳受，得曲而不用之於宗廟朝廷也。

translations.literal: Although the Qi regime knew how to transmit and receive them, having obtained the pieces they did not use them in the ancestral temple or at court.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi court knew how to preserve and pass them on, yet though it possessed the pieces, it never performed them in the ancestral temple or at court.

sentences.zh: 臣少好音律，留意管弦，年雖耆老，頗皆記憶。

translations.literal: Your subject has loved music and pitch since youth and attended closely to strings and pipes; though now advanced in years, I remember them fairly well.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has loved music and pitch since youth and kept close watch over strings and pipes; though I am now old, I remember them fairly well.

sentences.zh: 及東土克定，樂人悉返，訪其逗遛，果雲是梁人所教。

translations.literal: When the eastern lands were pacified, musicians all returned; inquiring into their lingering traces, it was indeed said they had been taught by men of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern lands were pacified, the musicians all returned; on inquiry it proved that they had indeed been taught by men of Liang.

sentences.zh: 今三調、四儛並皆有手，雖不能精熟，亦頗具雅聲。

translations.literal: Now for the three modes and four dances there are masters at hand; though not fully proficient, they still preserve much of the refined sound.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are still masters of the three modes and four dances; though not perfectly skilled, they preserve much of the refined court sound.

sentences.zh: 若令教習傳授，庶得流傳古樂。

translations.literal: If instruction and transmission were ordered, ancient music might yet be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If they were taught and handed down, the ancient music might yet survive.

sentences.zh: 然後取其會歸，撮其指要，因循損益，更制嘉名。

translations.literal: Then gathering their essential principles and extracting their key points, following precedent while adding and subtracting, new worthy names could be devised.
translations.idiomatic: Then, gathering their essential principles and distilling their core points, one could follow precedent while refining them and bestowing new worthy titles.

sentences.zh: 歌盛德於當今，傳雅正于來葉，豈不美與！

translations.literal: To sing the flourishing virtue of the present age and transmit refined orthodoxy to later generations—would this not be fine!
translations.idiomatic: To sing the present age's flourishing virtue and pass refined orthodoxy to later generations—what could be finer!

sentences.zh: 謹具錄三調、四舞曲名，又制歌辭如別。

translations.literal: I respectfully append a full record of the names of the three modes and four dances, and have also composed song texts separately.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit a full list of the three modes and four dances, with song texts composed separately as an appendix.

sentences.zh: 其有聲曲流宕，不可以陳於殿庭者，亦悉附之於後。

translations.literal: Those pieces whose melodies are unrestrained and cannot be presented in the hall of audience are also all appended at the end.
translations.idiomatic: Pieces whose melodies are too unrestrained for presentation in the imperial hall are also appended at the end.

sentences.zh: 書奏，別敕太常取妥節度。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, a separate edict ordered the Director of Ceremonial to adopt Tuo's measures.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, a separate edict ordered the Director of Ceremonial to follow Tuo's plan.

sentences.zh: 於是作清、平、瑟三調聲，又作八佾、《鞞》、《鐸》、《巾》、《拂》四舞。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three modes—qing, ping, and se—were composed, along with the eight-row dance and the four dances Bian, Duo, Jin, and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the three modes qing, ping, and se were established, together with the eight-row dance and the four dances Bian, Duo, Jin, and Fu.

sentences.zh: 先是，太常所傳宗廟雅樂，數十年唯作大呂，廢黃鐘。

translations.literal: Previously, in the ancestral temple music transmitted by the Director of Ceremonial, for decades only the great lü was used and the yellow bell was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in the ancestral temple music preserved by the Director of Ceremonial, the court had for decades used only the great lü and abandoned the yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 妥又以深乖古意，乃奏請用黃鐘。

translations.literal: Tuo also considered this a deep violation of ancient intent and memorialized requesting use of the yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo considered this a grave departure from ancient practice and memorialized requesting restoration of the yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 詔下公卿議，從之。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for discussion among high officials, and they agreed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was sent down for deliberation among the high officials, and they assented.

sentences.zh: 俄而妥子蔚為秘書郎，有罪當刑，上哀之，減死論。

translations.literal: Soon after, Tuo's son Wei served as secretary; guilty of a crime meriting punishment, the emperor pitied him and reduced the sentence from death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Tuo's son Wei, serving as a secretary, was guilty of a capital offense; the emperor took pity on him and commuted the death sentence.

sentences.zh: 是後恩禮漸薄。

translations.literal: After this, imperial favor gradually grew thin.
translations.idiomatic: After that, imperial favor toward him gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 六年，出為龍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was sent out as prefect of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was posted out as prefect of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 時有負笈遊學者，妥皆為講說教授之。

translations.literal: At that time scholars traveling with book bundles came to study; Tuo lectured and instructed them all.
translations.idiomatic: When traveling scholars arrived with book bundles, Tuo lectured and taught them all.

sentences.zh: 為《刺史箴》，勒於州門外。

translations.literal: He composed an "Admonition for a Prefect" and had it carved outside the prefectural gate.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote an "Admonition for a Prefect" and had it inscribed outside the prefectural gate.

sentences.zh: 在職三年，以疾請還，詔許之。

translations.literal: After three years in office he requested return on grounds of illness, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he asked to return home on account of illness, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 復知學事。

translations.literal: He again supervised academic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again took charge of academic affairs.

sentences.zh: 時上方使蘇夔在太常，參議鐘律。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had assigned Su Kui to the Director of Ceremonial to consult on bells and pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had Su Kui serve under the Director of Ceremonial to deliberate on bells and pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 夔有所建議，朝士多從之，妥獨不同，每言夔之短。

translations.literal: When Kui made proposals, most court officials followed him; Tuo alone disagreed and often spoke of Kui's shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui put forward proposals, most court officials sided with him; Tuo alone dissented and often criticized Kui's faults.

sentences.zh: 高祖下其議，朝臣多排妥。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu circulated the proposal for discussion, and many court officials sided against Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu circulated Kui's proposal for debate, and most court officials turned against Tuo.

sentences.zh: 妥復上封事，指陳得失，大抵論時政損益，並指斥當世朋黨。

translations.literal: Tuo again submitted a sealed memorial detailing gains and losses, largely discussing what should be added or removed in current policy, and also denouncing factions of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Tuo again submitted a sealed memorial setting forth what should be kept and what discarded in current policy, and denouncing the factions of the day.

sentences.zh: 於是蘇威及吏部尚書盧愷、侍郎薛道衡等皆坐得罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Lu Kai, Vice-Minister Xue Daoheng, and others were all convicted on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Su Wei, Minister of Personnel Lu Kai, Vice-Minister Xue Daoheng, and others were all punished on account of it.

sentences.zh: 除伊州刺史，不行，尋為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Yizhou but did not go; soon after he became Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Yizhou but declined to go; soon afterward he was made Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Su ("Solemn").
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Su ("Solemn").

sentences.zh: 撰《周易講疏》十三卷，《孝經義疏》三卷，《莊子義疏》四卷，及與沈重等撰《三十六科鬼神感應等大義》九卷，《封禪書》一卷，《樂要》一卷，文集十卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He compiled Commentaries on the Zhou Changes in thirteen scrolls, Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety in three scrolls, and Exegesis of the Zhuangzi in four scrolls; together with Shen Chong and others he compiled Great Themes on Thirty-Six Categories of Spirit Manifestations in nine scrolls; one scroll each of Book of the Feng and Shan Sacrifices and Essentials of Music; and ten scrolls of collected writings—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Commentaries on the Zhou Changes in thirteen scrolls, Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety in three scrolls, and Exegesis of the Zhuangzi in four scrolls; with Shen Chong and others he compiled Great Themes on Thirty-Six Categories of Spirit Manifestations in nine scrolls; one scroll each on the Feng and Shan sacrifices and on the essentials of music; and ten scrolls of collected writings—all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 蘭陵蕭該者，梁鄱陽王恢之孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Gai of Lanling was a grandson of Xiao Hui, Prince of Poyang of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Gai of Lanling was a grandson of Xiao Hui, Prince of Poyang of Liang.

sentences.zh: 少封攸侯。

translations.literal: In youth he was enfeoffed as Marquis of You.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was enfeoffed as Marquis of You.

sentences.zh: 梁荊州陷，與何妥同至長安。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou of Liang fell, he arrived at Chang'an together with He Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Jingzhou fell, he fled to Chang'an together with He Tuo.

sentences.zh: 性篤學，《詩》、《書》、《春秋》、《禮記》並通大義，尤精《漢書》，甚為貴遊所禮。

translations.literal: By nature deeply studious, he mastered the broad sense of the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites, and was especially expert in the Book of Han, highly esteemed by the nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted to learning by nature, he grasped the broad meaning of the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn, and Record of Rites, and was especially expert in the Book of Han; the high nobility held him in great esteem.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，賜爵山陰縣公，拜國子博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was granted the title Duke of Shanyin County and appointed Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang reign he was granted the title Duke of Shanyin County and appointed an erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 奉詔書與妥正定經史，然各執所見，遞相是非，久而不能就，上譴而罷之。

translations.literal: By imperial command he was ordered to work with Tuo to fix the classics and histories; yet each clung to his own views and contradicted the other in turn; after long failure to finish, the emperor rebuked them and dismissed the project.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he and Tuo were charged with fixing the classics and histories, but each clung to his own views and contradicted the other; after long delay with no result, the emperor rebuked them and called the project off.

sentences.zh: 該後撰《漢書》及《文選》音義，咸為當時所貴。

translations.literal: Gai later compiled phonological glosses on the Book of Han and the Wen Xuan, both highly prized at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Gai later compiled phonological glosses on the Book of Han and the Wen Xuan, both highly prized in his day.

sentences.zh: 東海包愷，字和樂。

translations.literal: Bao Kai of Donghai, courtesy name Hele.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Kai of Donghai, courtesy name Hele.

sentences.zh: 其兄愉，明《五經》，愷悉傳其業。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yu was expert in the Five Classics; Kai fully inherited his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yu was expert in the Five Classics, and Kai fully inherited his learning.

sentences.zh: 又從王仲通受《史記》、《漢書》，尤稱精究。

translations.literal: He also studied the Records of the Grand Historian and Book of Han under Wang Zhongtong, and was especially renowned for thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied the Records of the Grand Historian and the Book of Han under Wang Zhongtong, and was especially renowned for his thorough mastery.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為國子助教。

translations.literal: During the Daye reign he served as assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he served as an assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 于時《漢書》學者，以蕭、包二人為宗匠。

translations.literal: At that time among scholars of the Book of Han, Xiao and Bao were regarded as the master craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: At that time scholars of the Book of Han looked to Xiao and Bao as the leading masters of the field.

sentences.zh: 聚徒教授，著錄者數千人，卒，門人為起墳立碣焉。

translations.literal: He gathered disciples to teach; registered students numbered in the thousands; when he died, his disciples raised a tomb and erected a stele for him.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered disciples to teach, with registered students numbering in the thousands; when he died, his disciples raised his tomb and set up a stele.

sentences.zh: 房暉遠房暉遠，字崇儒，恆山真定人也。

translations.literal: Fang Huiyuan. Fang Huiyuan, courtesy name Chongru, was a native of Zhending in Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Huiyuan. Fang Huiyuan, courtesy name Chongru, was a native of Zhending in Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 世傳儒學。

translations.literal: His family had transmitted Confucian learning for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian learning had been handed down in his family for generations.

sentences.zh: 暉遠幼有志行，治《三禮》、《春秋三傳》、《詩》、《書》、《周易》，兼善圖緯，恆以教授為務。

translations.literal: Huiyuan from youth had resolve and conduct; he studied the Three Rites, the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, the Odes, Documents, and Zhou Changes, and was also skilled in apocryphal cosmology—teaching was his constant task.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huiyuan had strong moral resolve; he studied the Three Rites, the Three Commentaries on the Spring and Autumn, the Odes, Documents, and Zhou Changes, and was also versed in apocryphal cosmology—teaching was his lifelong calling.

sentences.zh: 遠方負笈而從者，動以千計。

translations.literal: Students coming from afar with book bundles numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came from afar with book bundles numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 齊南陽王綽為定州刺史，聞其名，召為博士。

translations.literal: When Chuo, Prince of Nanyang of Northern Qi, was prefect of Dingzhou, hearing his reputation he summoned him as erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo, Prince of Nanyang of Northern Qi, served as prefect of Dingzhou, he heard of Huiyuan's reputation and summoned him as an erudite.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，搜訪儒俊，暉遠首應辟命，授小學下士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, seeking out Confucian talents, Huiyuan was first to answer the summons and was appointed lower gentleman of the Minor Learning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi and sought out Confucian talent, Huiyuan was the first to answer the summons and was appointed a lower gentleman of the Minor Learning.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was promoted to erudite of the Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Huiyuan was promoted to erudite under the Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 太常卿牛弘每稱為五經庫。

translations.literal: Director of Ceremonial Niu Hong often called him a treasury of the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Ceremonial Niu Hong often called him a living treasury of the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書韋世康薦之，為太學博士。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wei Shikang recommended him, and he became erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wei Shikang recommended him, and he was appointed an erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 尋與沛公鄭譯修正樂章。

translations.literal: Soon after he joined Duke of Pei Zheng Yi in revising ceremonial music.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he joined Duke of Pei Zheng Yi in revising the ceremonial music.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，解任。

translations.literal: Upon mourning his mother, he resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he resigned his office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，授殄寇將軍，復為太常博士。

translations.literal: Several years later he was appointed General for Punishing Bandits and again served as erudite of the Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was appointed General for Punishing Bandits and again served as an erudite under the Director of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢為國子博士。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會上令國子生通一經者，並悉薦舉，將擢用之。

translations.literal: It happened that the emperor ordered that all academy students who had mastered one classic were to be recommended for selection and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the emperor ordered all academy students who had mastered one classic to be recommended for selection and promotion.

sentences.zh: 既策問訖，博士不能時定臧否。

translations.literal: After the examination by question was finished, the erudites could not promptly decide who passed or failed.
translations.idiomatic: After the written examination was finished, the erudites could not promptly decide who had passed or failed.

sentences.zh: 祭酒元善怪問之，暉遠曰：「江南、河北，義例不同，博士不能遍涉。

translations.literal: Director Yuan Shan wondered at this and questioned him; Huiyuan said: "South of the Yangtze and north of the Yellow River follow different exegetical conventions—the erudites cannot cover them all.
translations.idiomatic: Director Yuan Shan found this strange and questioned him; Huiyuan said: "South of the Yangtze and north of the Yellow River follow different exegetical conventions, and the erudites cannot master them all.

sentences.zh: 學生皆持其所短，稱己所長，博士各各自疑，所以久而不決也。」

translations.literal: Each student seized on others' weak points and praised his own strengths; each erudite was uncertain in turn—hence the long delay in reaching a decision."
translations.idiomatic: Each student seized on others' weaknesses and praised his own strengths; each erudite was left in doubt—hence the long delay in reaching a verdict.

sentences.zh: 祭酒因令暉遠考定之，暉遠覽筆便下，初無疑滯。

translations.literal: The Director thereupon had Huiyuan assess and decide; Huiyuan read through and wrote his verdict at once, without hesitation from the start.
translations.idiomatic: The Director then had Huiyuan assess and decide the cases; Huiyuan read through the papers and wrote his verdicts at once, without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 或有不服者，暉遠問其所傳義疏，輒為始末誦之，然後出其所短，自是無敢飾非者。

translations.literal: When any were dissatisfied, Huiyuan asked which commentary tradition they followed and would recite it from beginning to end, then point out their errors—after which none dared conceal their faults.
translations.idiomatic: When any student objected, Huiyuan asked which commentary tradition he followed and would recite it from beginning to end, then expose his errors—after which none dared conceal his faults.

sentences.zh: 所試四五百人，數日便決，諸儒莫不推其通博，皆自以為不能測也。

translations.literal: For four or five hundred candidates examined, the decision was made within days; all the scholars praised his breadth of mastery, each confessing he could not measure his depth.
translations.idiomatic: For four or five hundred candidates, the verdicts were settled within days; every scholar praised his breadth of learning, each admitting he could not fathom his depth.

sentences.zh: 尋奉詔預修令式。

translations.literal: Soon after he received an imperial order to take part in compiling statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he received an imperial order to take part in compiling statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗謂群臣曰：「自古天子有女樂乎？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once said to his assembled ministers: "Since antiquity, have Sons of Heaven ever had female musicians?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu once asked his assembled ministers: "Since antiquity, have emperors ever kept female musicians?

sentences.zh: 楊素以下莫知所出，遂言無女樂。

translations.literal: Those from Yang Su downward did not know what to answer, and so said there were no female musicians.
translations.idiomatic: From Yang Su on down, no one knew how to reply, and they all said there were no female musicians.

sentences.zh: 暉遠進曰：「臣聞'窈窕淑女，鐘鼓樂之'，此即王者房中之樂，著於《雅頌》，不得言無。」

translations.literal: Huiyuan stepped forward and said: "Your servant has heard, 'Fair is the modest maiden—strike bells and drums to rejoice her'—this is music for the king within his chambers, recorded in the Hymns and Eulogies; one cannot say there were none."
translations.idiomatic: Huiyuan stepped forward and said: "Your servant has heard, 'The fair and modest maiden—bells and drums rejoice her'—this is the music a ruler keeps within his chambers, recorded in the Hymns and Eulogies; one cannot say there were none.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中卒官，時年七十二，朝廷嗟惜焉，賵賻甚厚，贈員外散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he died in office, aged seventy-two; the court lamented him, gave lavish funeral gifts, and posthumously invested him as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he died in office at the age of seventy-two; the court mourned his loss, sent lavish funeral gifts, and posthumously invested him as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 馬光馬光，字榮伯，武安人也。

translations.literal: Ma Guang—Ma Guang, styled Rongbo, was a native of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Guang, styled Rongbo, was a native of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 少好學，從師數十年，晝夜不息，圖書讖緯，莫不畢覽，尤明《三禮》，為儒者所宗。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; following teachers for decades, day and night without rest, books, charts, and apocryphal texts—none he did not thoroughly read; he was especially versed in the Three Rites and was revered by Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; he studied under teachers for decades without rest day or night, and thoroughly read books, charts, and apocryphal texts; he was especially versed in the Three Rites and was revered by Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，高祖征山東義學之士，光與張仲讓、孔籠、竇士榮、張黑奴、劉祖仁等俱至，並授太學博士，時人號為六儒。

translations.literal: In early Kaihuang, Gaozu summoned righteous scholars of the east beyond the mountains; Guang together with Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, Dou Shirong, Zhang Heinu, Liu Zuren, and others all arrived and were all appointed erudites of the Imperial University—the men of the time called them the Six Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era, Gaozu summoned righteous scholars from east of the mountains; Guang arrived together with Zhang Zhongrang, Kong Long, Dou Shirong, Zhang Heinu, Liu Zuren, and others, and they were all appointed erudites of the Imperial University—the age called them the Six Confucians.

sentences.zh: 然皆鄙野無儀範，朝廷不之貴也。

translations.literal: Yet all were coarse and uncouth, without decorum; the court did not hold them in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were all crude and uncouth, lacking proper bearing, and the court did not regard them highly.

sentences.zh: 士榮尋病死。

translations.literal: Shirong soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 仲讓未幾告歸鄉里，著書十卷，自雲此書若奏，我必為宰相。

translations.literal: Zhongrang before long asked leave to return home, wrote a book in ten scrolls, and declared himself that if this book were submitted, he would surely become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongrang asked leave to return home, wrote a ten-scroll book, and declared that if it were submitted to the throne, he would surely become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 又數言玄象事。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly spoke of celestial signs and portents.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly spoke of celestial omens and portents.

sentences.zh: 州縣列上其狀，竟坐誅。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county submitted reports on his conduct; in the end he was executed for it.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county submitted reports on his conduct, and in the end he was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 孔籠、張黑奴、劉祖仁未幾亦被譴去。

translations.literal: Kong Long, Zhang Heinu, and Liu Zuren before long were also dismissed in disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Kong Long, Zhang Heinu, and Liu Zuren were also dismissed in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 唯光獨存。

translations.literal: Only Guang alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guang remained.

sentences.zh: 嘗因釋奠，高祖親幸國子學，王公以下畢集。

translations.literal: Once on the occasion of the sacrificial rite to Confucius, Gaozu personally visited the Imperial Academy; princes and dukes downward all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Once, at the Confucian sacrificial rite, Gaozu personally visited the Imperial Academy, and princes, dukes, and all ranks below them gathered.

sentences.zh: 光升座講禮，啟發章門。

translations.literal: Guang ascended the dais to lecture on ritual, opening and expounding passages and clauses.
translations.idiomatic: Guang ascended the lectern to expound ritual, opening passages and illuminating their meaning.

sentences.zh: 已而諸儒生以次論難者十餘人，皆當時碩學，光剖析疑滯，雖辭非俊辨，而理義弘贍，論者莫測其淺深，咸共推服，上嘉而勞焉。

translations.literal: Presently more than ten Confucian students in turn engaged in debate—all eminent scholars of the day; Guang dissected doubts and blockages; though his words were not brilliantly eloquent, his reasoning was broad and abundant; debaters could not measure his shallow or deep, and all together deferred to him; the emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Then more than ten Confucian students, all eminent scholars of the day, took turns debating with him; Guang resolved every doubt and difficulty. Though his speech was not brilliantly polished, his reasoning was broad and profound; none could plumb the full depth of his learning, and all deferred to him; the emperor praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 山東《三禮》學者，自熊安生後，唯宗光一人。

translations.literal: For Three Rites scholars east of the mountains, since Xiong Ansheng, only Guang alone was revered.
translations.idiomatic: Among Three Rites scholars east of the mountains, after Xiong Ansheng only Guang was revered.

sentences.zh: 初，教授瀛、博間，門徒千數，至是多負笈從入長安。

translations.literal: At first he taught between Ying and Bo; disciples numbered in the thousands; by this time many bearing book bundles followed him into Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At first he taught in the Ying and Bo region with disciples numbering in the thousands; by then many followed him to Chang'an with book bundles on their backs.

sentences.zh: 後數年，丁母憂歸鄉里，遂有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Several years later, upon mourning his mother he returned home and formed the resolve to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when his mother died he returned home to observe mourning and resolved to spend his remaining days there.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒于家，時年七十三。

translations.literal: He died of illness at home, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at home at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 劉焯劉焯，字士元，信都昌亭人也。

translations.literal: Liu Chuo—Liu Chuo, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Changting in Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo, styled Shiyuan, was a native of Changting in Xindu.

sentences.zh: 父洽，郡功曹。

translations.literal: His father He was a merit clerk of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father He served as merit clerk of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 焯犀額龜背，望高視遠，聰敏沈深，弱不好弄。

translations.literal: Chuo had a prominent forehead like a rhinoceros and a tortoise-shell back; he looked high and saw far; he was clever, keen, and profound; as a child he did not care for play.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo had a prominent brow and a broad back; his gaze was elevated and far-reaching; he was clever, keen, and profoundly thoughtful; as a child he had no taste for play.

sentences.zh: 少與河間劉炫結盟為友，同受《詩》于同郡劉軌思，受《左傳》于廣平郭懋常，問《禮》于阜城熊安生，皆不卒業而去。

translations.literal: In youth he formed a sworn friendship with Liu Xuan of Hejian; both studied the Odes under Liu Guisi of the same commandery, the Zuo Commentary under Guo Maochang of Guangping, and inquired into the Rites under Xiong Ansheng of Fucheng—but left each without completing the course.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he formed a sworn friendship with Liu Xuan of Hejian; together they studied the Odes under Liu Guisi of the same commandery, the Zuo Commentary under Guo Maochang of Guangping, and inquired into the Rites under Xiong Ansheng of Fucheng—but left each without finishing.

sentences.zh: 武強交津橋劉智海家素多墳籍，焯與炫就之讀書，向經十載，雖衣食不繼，晏如也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhihai of Jiaojin Bridge in Wuqiang had in his household many ancient tomes; Chuo and Xuan went to him to read, facing the classics for ten years; though food and clothing did not follow, they were content.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhihai of Jiaojin Bridge in Wuqiang kept many ancient texts in his home; Chuo and Xuan went there to study and spent ten years immersed in the classics; though they often lacked food and clothing, they remained entirely content.

sentences.zh: 遂以儒學知名，為州博士。

translations.literal: He thereby became renowned for Confucian learning and served as erudite of the province.
translations.idiomatic: He thereby became renowned for Confucian learning and was appointed provincial erudite.

sentences.zh: 刺史趙煚引為從事，舉秀才，射策甲科。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhao Kai summoned him as an aide, recommended him as an Outstanding Talent, and he placed in Grade A on the target-shooting examination.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhao Kai summoned him as an aide, recommended him as an Outstanding Talent, and he placed in Grade A on the civil examination.

sentences.zh: 與著作郎王劭同修國史，兼參議律曆，仍直門下省，以待顧問。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Shao, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Compilation, he revised the dynastic history; he also participated in deliberating on law and calendar, and continued attached to the Chancellery to await consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Shao, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Compilation, he revised the dynastic history; he also participated in deliberations on law and the calendar, and was attached to the Chancellery to await imperial consultation.

sentences.zh: 俄除員外將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed supernumerary general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed supernumerary general.

sentences.zh: 後與諸儒于秘書省考定群言。

translations.literal: Later, together with various Confucians, he examined and established the meaning of various texts at the Secretariat Library.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined various Confucian scholars at the Secretariat Library in examining and establishing the meaning of classical texts.

sentences.zh: 因假還鄉里，縣令韋之業引為功曹。

translations.literal: On leave returning home, Magistrate Wei Zhiye summoned him as merit clerk.
translations.idiomatic: While on leave in his home district, Magistrate Wei Zhiye summoned him as merit clerk.

sentences.zh: 尋復入京，與左僕射楊素、吏部尚書牛弘、國子祭酒蘇威、國子祭酒元善、博士蕭該、何妥、太學博士房暉遠、崔宗德、晉王文學崔賾等於國子共論古今滯義前賢所不通者。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to the capital and, together with Left Vice-Director Yang Su, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Imperial Academy Directors Su Wei and Yuan Shan, erudites Xiao Gai and He Tuo, Imperial University erudites Fang Huiyuan and Cui Zongde, and Literature Aide to the Prince of Jin Cui Yi and others, at the Imperial Academy jointly debated obscure passages of past and present that the former worthies had not penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to the capital and at the Imperial Academy debated with Left Vice-Director Yang Su, Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, Academy Directors Su Wei and Yuan Shan, erudites Xiao Gai and He Tuo, Imperial University erudites Fang Huiyuan and Cui Zongde, Literature Aide to the Prince of Jin Cui Yi, and others on obscure passages of past and present that earlier masters had not resolved.

sentences.zh: 每升座，論難鋒起，皆不能屈，楊素等莫不服其精博。

translations.literal: Each time he ascended the seat, debate flared like blades; none could bend him; Yang Su and the others all submitted to his profound breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he took the floor, debate flared fiercely, yet none could refute him; Yang Su and the others all marveled at his profound erudition.

sentences.zh: 六年，運洛陽《石經》至京師，文字磨滅，莫能知者，奉敕與劉炫等考定。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the Stone Classics from Luoyang were transported to the capital, the characters were worn away and none could read them; by imperial order he and Liu Xuan and others examined and established their text.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the Stone Classics from Luoyang were transported to the capital with their characters worn away beyond legibility, he received an imperial order to examine and establish their text together with Liu Xuan and others.

sentences.zh: 後因國子釋奠，與炫二人論義，深挫諸儒，咸懷妒恨，遂為飛章所謗，除名為民。

translations.literal: Later, on the occasion of the Imperial Academy sacrificial rite, he and Xuan the two of them debated doctrine and deeply humbled the other scholars; all harbored jealousy and resentment; he was then slandered by anonymous memorial and dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the Imperial Academy Confucian rite, he and Xuan debated doctrine together and thoroughly humbled the other scholars; all were consumed with envy, and he was slandered by anonymous memorial and stripped of office to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 於是優遊鄉里，專以教授著述為務，孜孜不倦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wandered at ease in his home district, devoting himself solely to teaching and writing, never weary.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he lived at ease in his home district, devoting himself solely to teaching and writing without rest.

sentences.zh: 賈、馬、王、鄭所傳章句，多所是非。

translations.literal: The commentarial traditions transmitted by Jia, Ma, Wang, and Zheng—on many points he affirmed or rejected.
translations.idiomatic: On the commentarial traditions of Jia, Ma, Wang, and Zheng, he frequently took sides, affirming some passages and rejecting others.

sentences.zh: 《九章算術》、《周髀》、《七曜曆書》十餘部，推步日月之經，量度山海之術，莫不核其根本，窮其秘奧。

translations.literal: More than ten works including the Nine Chapters on Mathematical Procedures, the Zhou Bi, and the Seven Luminaries Calendar Texts—in calculating the paths of sun and moon, and in techniques for measuring mountains and seas—none did he fail to verify at the root and exhaust in hidden depths.
translations.idiomatic: Among more than ten works including the Nine Chapters on Mathematical Procedures, the Zhou Bi, and the Seven Luminaries Calendar Texts, whether calculating the courses of sun and moon or measuring mountains and seas, he verified every fundamental principle and pursued every hidden subtlety.

sentences.zh: 著《稽極》十卷，《曆書》十卷，《五經述議》，並行於世。

translations.literal: He authored Verification of the Ultimate in ten scrolls, Calendar Book in ten scrolls, and Discussions on the Five Classics—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Verification of the Ultimate in ten scrolls, Calendar Book in ten scrolls, and Discussions on the Five Classics—all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 劉炫聰明博學，名亞於焯，故時人稱二劉焉。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan was bright and broadly learned; his reputation was second to Chuo's—hence men of the time called them the Two Lius.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was brilliant and broadly learned; his reputation was second only to Chuo's, and men of the time called them the Two Lius.

sentences.zh: 天下名儒後進，質疑受業，不遠千里而至者，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Famed Confucians and rising students from across the realm, questioning and receiving instruction—those who came from a thousand li away were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Famed Confucian masters and rising students from across the realm came to question him and receive instruction; those who traveled a thousand li or more were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 論者以為數百年已來，博學通儒，無能出其右者。

translations.literal: Commentators held that for several hundred years there had been no broadly learned thorough Confucian who could surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that for several hundred years no broadly learned Confucian had surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 然懷抱不曠，又嗇於財，不行束修者，未嘗有所教誨，時人以此少之。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing was not broad-minded, and he was also stingy with wealth; those who did not present the customary teacher's gift—he never instructed them—men of the time therefore thought less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was narrow in temperament and stingy with money; those who did not bring the customary teacher's gift never received instruction, and for this men of the time thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 廢太子勇聞而召之，未及進謁，詔令事蜀王，非其好也，久之不至。

translations.literal: Deposed Crown Prince Yong heard of him and summoned him; before he could present himself at court, an edict ordered him to serve the Prince of Shu—this was not to his liking, and for a long time he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Crown Prince Yong heard of him and summoned him; before he could present himself at court, an edict ordered him to serve the Prince of Shu—which did not suit him, and for a long time he failed to go.

sentences.zh: 王聞而大怒，遣人枷送於蜀，配之軍防。

translations.literal: The prince heard of this and was greatly angered; he sent men to shackle and transport him to Shu and assigned him to military guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: The prince heard of this and was furious; he sent men to shackle him and transport him to Shu, assigning him to military guard duty.

sentences.zh: 其後典校書籍。

translations.literal: Later he was put in charge of collating books.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was put in charge of collating books.

sentences.zh: 王以罪廢，焯又與諸儒修定禮律，除雲騎尉。

translations.literal: When the prince was deposed for crime, Chuo again joined the Confucians in revising rites and law, and was appointed Cloud Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince was deposed for his crimes, Chuo again joined the Confucian scholars in revising rites and law and was appointed Cloud Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷太學博士，俄以疾去職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he was transferred to erudite of the Imperial University; soon he resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, he was transferred to erudite of the Imperial University; soon he resigned due to illness.

sentences.zh: 數年，復被征以待顧問，因上所著《曆書》，與太史令張胄玄多不同，被駁不用。

translations.literal: Several years later he was again summoned to await consultation; he submitted his authored Calendar Book, which differed greatly from that of Director of Astronomy Zhang Zhouxuan, and was rejected and not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was again summoned for imperial consultation; he submitted his Calendar Book, which differed greatly from that of Director of Astronomy Zhang Zhouxuan, and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 大業六年卒，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daye he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Daye at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 劉炫為之請諡，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan petitioned for a posthumous title for him; the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan petitioned for a posthumous title for him, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 劉炫劉炫，字光伯，河間景城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan—Liu Xuan, styled Guangbo, was a native of Jingcheng in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan, styled Guangbo, was a native of Jingcheng in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少以聰敏見稱，與信都劉焯閉戶讀書，十年不出。

translations.literal: From youth he was praised for cleverness and keenness; with Liu Chuo of Xindu he shut the door and read books, not going out for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was praised for brilliance; with Liu Chuo of Xindu he shut himself indoors to study and did not go out for ten years.

sentences.zh: 炫眸子精明，視日不眩，強記默識，莫與為儔。

translations.literal: Xuan's pupils were bright and keen; he could look at the sun without dazzlement; his memory and silent retention had no peer.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's eyes were sharp and clear; he could gaze at the sun without being dazzled; his memory was unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 左畫方，右畫圓，口誦，目數，耳聽，五事同舉，無有遺失。

translations.literal: With his left hand he drew a square, with his right a circle; with his mouth he recited, with his eyes he counted, with his ears he listened—five tasks at once, with nothing lost.
translations.idiomatic: He could draw a square with his left hand and a circle with his right, recite aloud, count with his eyes, and listen with his ears—all five tasks at once, without missing anything.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，瀛州刺史宇文亢引為戶曹從事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, Yingzhou Prefect Yuwen Kang summoned him as an aide in the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Yingzhou Prefect Yuwen Kang summoned him as an aide in the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 後刺史李繪署禮曹從事，以吏幹知名。

translations.literal: Later Prefect Li Hui appointed him aide in the Rites Bureau; he became known for administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prefect Li Hui appointed him aide in the Rites Bureau, and he became known for his administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，奉敕與著作郎王劭同修國史。

translations.literal: After a year and more, by imperial order he joined Wang Shao, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Compilation, in revising the dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, he received an imperial order to join Wang Shao, Gentleman of the Secretariat for Compilation, in revising the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 俄直門下省，以待顧問。

translations.literal: Soon he was attached to the Chancellery to await consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was attached to the Chancellery to await imperial consultation.

sentences.zh: 又與諸術者修天文律曆，兼于內史省考定群言，內史令博陵李德林甚禮之。

translations.literal: He also joined various specialists in revising astronomy, law, and calendar, and concurrently at the Imperial Secretariat examined and established various texts; Secretariat Director Li Delin of Boling treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined various specialists in revising astronomy, law, and the calendar, and concurrently examined and established classical texts at the Imperial Secretariat; Secretariat Director Li Delin of Boling treated him with great respect.

sentences.zh: 炫雖遍直三省，竟不得官，為縣司責其賦役。

translations.literal: Though Xuan was attached across all three departments, in the end he received no office; the county authorities pressed him for tax and corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xuan served on attachment across all three central departments, he never received an official appointment; the county authorities pressed him for tax and corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 炫自陳于內史，內史送詣吏部，吏部尚書韋世康問其所能。

translations.literal: Xuan presented his case to the Imperial Secretariat; the Secretariat sent him to the Ministry of Personnel; Minister Wei Shikang asked what he could do.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan presented his case to the Imperial Secretariat, which referred him to the Ministry of Personnel; Minister Wei Shikang asked what he was capable of.

sentences.zh: 炫自為狀曰：「《周禮》、《禮記》、《毛詩》、《尚書》、《公羊》、《左傳》、《孝經》、《論語》孔、鄭、王、何、服、杜等注，凡十三家，雖義有精粗，並堪講授。

translations.literal: Xuan wrote his own petition saying: "The Zhou Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, Documents, Gongyang Commentary, Zuo Commentary, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects—commentaries of Kong, Zheng, Wang, He, Fu, Du, and others, thirteen traditions in all—though the interpretations vary in refinement, all are fit for teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a written statement saying: "The Zhou Rites, Record of Rites, Mao Odes, Documents, Gongyang Commentary, Zuo Commentary, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects—the commentaries of Kong, Zheng, Wang, He, Fu, Du, and others, thirteen traditions in all—though varying in refinement, are all fit for me to lecture on.

sentences.zh: 《周易》、《儀禮》、《谷梁》，用功差少。

translations.literal: The Zhou Changes, Ceremonial Rites, and Guliang Commentary—I have applied somewhat less effort to these.
translations.idiomatic: I have devoted somewhat less effort to the Zhou Changes, Ceremonial Rites, and Guliang Commentary.

sentences.zh: 史子文集，嘉言美事，咸誦於心。

translations.literal: Historical, philosophical, and collected writings—fine words and fine deeds—I have memorized them all in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Historical, philosophical, and collected writings—fine words and fine deeds—I have memorized them all.

sentences.zh: 天文律曆，窮核微妙。

translations.literal: Astronomy, law, and calendar—I have exhausted and verified their subtle points.
translations.idiomatic: In astronomy, law, and the calendar, I have pursued every subtle point to its root.

sentences.zh: 至於公私文翰，未嘗假手。」

translations.literal: As for public and private documents, I have never needed another's hand."
translations.idiomatic: As for drafting official or private documents, I have never needed anyone else's help.

sentences.zh: 吏部竟不詳試，然在朝知名之士十餘人，保明炫所陳不謬，於是除殿內將軍。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel never examined him in detail, but more than ten renowned men at court vouched that what Xuan stated was not false; thereupon he was appointed Palace Interior General.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel never tested him in detail, but more than ten renowned men at court vouched that Xuan's claims were accurate, and he was appointed Palace Interior General.

sentences.zh: 時牛弘奏請購求天下遺逸之書，炫遂偽造書百餘卷，題為《連山易》、《魯史記》等，錄上送官，取賞而去。

translations.literal: At the time Niu Hong memorialized requesting purchase and search for lost books throughout the realm; Xuan then forged more than a hundred scrolls, titled them Linked Mountains Changes, Records of the State of Lu, and the like, copied and submitted them to the authorities, received the reward, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Niu Hong memorialized requesting that lost books be sought and purchased throughout the realm; Xuan forged more than a hundred scrolls under titles such as Linked Mountains Changes and Records of the State of Lu, submitted them to the authorities, collected the reward, and left.

sentences.zh: 後有人訟之，經赦免死，坐除名，歸於家，以教授為務。

translations.literal: Later someone sued him; through amnesty he escaped death but was stripped of name and returned home, making teaching his task.
translations.idiomatic: Later someone exposed him; he was spared death through amnesty but stripped of office and sent home, devoting himself to teaching.

sentences.zh: 太子勇聞而召之，既至京師，敕令事蜀王秀，遷延不往。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong heard of him and summoned him; once he reached the capital, an edict ordered him to serve Prince of Shu Xiu; he delayed and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong heard of him and summoned him; once he reached the capital, an edict ordered him to serve Prince of Shu Xiu, but he delayed and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 蜀王大怒，枷送益州。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu was greatly angered and had him shackled and sent to Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu was furious and had him shackled and sent to Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 既而配為帳內，每使執杖為門衛。

translations.literal: Presently he was assigned as a tent guard; each day they made him hold a staff as a gate guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was then assigned as a tent guard and made to stand at the gate holding a staff.

sentences.zh: 俄而釋之，典校書史。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and put in charge of collating books and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was released and put in charge of collating books and histories.

sentences.zh: 炫因擬屈原《卜居》，為《筮途》以自寄。

translations.literal: Xuan thereupon modeled himself on Qu Yuan's Divining the Dwelling Place and composed Divining the Road as a vehicle for his own feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then modeled himself on Qu Yuan's Divining the Dwelling Place and composed Divining the Road to express his own plight.

sentences.zh: 及蜀王廢，與諸儒修定《五禮》，授旅騎尉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Shu was deposed, he joined the Confucians in revising and establishing the Five Rites, and was appointed Traveling Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Shu was deposed, he joined the Confucian scholars in revising the Five Rites and was appointed Traveling Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書牛弘建議，以為禮諸侯絕傍期，大夫降一等。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Niu Hong proposed that, according to rites, feudal lords cut off collateral mourning at one remove, and grand masters reduce mourning by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Niu Hong proposed that, according to ritual, feudal lords cut off collateral mourning at one remove, and grand masters reduce mourning obligations by one grade.

sentences.zh: 今之上柱國，雖不同古諸侯，比大夫可也，官在第二品，宜降傍親一等。

translations.literal: Today's Superior Pillar of the State, though not the same as feudal lords of old, may be compared to grand masters; his office is of the second rank—it is fitting to reduce mourning for collateral relatives by one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Superior Pillar of the State, though not identical to the feudal lords of old, is comparable to a grand master; as a second-rank official, mourning for collateral relatives should be reduced by one grade.

sentences.zh: 議者多以為然。

translations.literal: Most of those debating thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those debating agreed.

sentences.zh: 炫駁之曰：「古之仕者，宗一人而已，庶子不得進。

translations.literal: Xuan rebutted, saying: "Office-holders of old advanced only one man from the lineage; secondary sons could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rebutted, saying: "In antiquity only one man from a lineage held office; secondary sons could not advance.

sentences.zh: 由是先王重適，其宗子有分祿之義。

translations.literal: Hence the former kings emphasized the heir; the lineage head had the principle of apportioned stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the former kings emphasized the legitimate heir; the lineage head had the principle of shared stipends.

sentences.zh: 族人與宗子雖疏遠，猶服縗三月，良由受其恩也。

translations.literal: Clansmen and the lineage head, though distant in relation, still wore hemp mourning for three months—truly because they received his bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen and the lineage head, though distant in kinship, still wore hemp mourning for three months—because they benefited from his bounty.

sentences.zh: 今之仕者，位以才升，不限適庶，與古既異，何降之有。

translations.literal: Today's office-holders rise by talent, without limit to heir or secondary son—already different from antiquity; why any reduction?
translations.idiomatic: Today's office-holders rise by talent, without regard to heir or secondary son—already unlike antiquity; why should mourning be reduced?

sentences.zh: 今之貴者，多忽近親，若或降之，民德之疏，自此始矣。」

translations.literal: Today's lofty men mostly neglect near kin; if mourning were reduced, the loosening of popular virtue would begin here."
translations.idiomatic: Today's high officials mostly neglect close kin; if mourning were reduced, the loosening of popular virtue would begin here.

sentences.zh: 遂寢其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 開皇二十年，廢國子四門及州縣學，唯置太學博士二人，學生七十二人。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang, the Four Gates of the Imperial Academy and prefectural and county schools were abolished; only two erudites of the Imperial University and seventy-two students were retained.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaihuang, the Four Gates of the Imperial Academy and the prefectural and county schools were abolished; only two Imperial University erudites and seventy-two students were retained.

sentences.zh: 炫上表言學校不宜廢，情理甚切，高祖不納。

translations.literal: Xuan submitted a memorial saying schools should not be abolished; his reasoning was very urgent—but Gaozu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan submitted a memorial arguing that schools should not be abolished; his reasoning was urgent and compelling, but Gaozu did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 開皇之末，國家殷盛，朝野皆以遼東為意。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, the state was prosperous; court and countryside alike had Liaodong in mind.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era, the state was prosperous, and court and countryside alike turned their thoughts to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 炫以為遼東不可伐，作《撫夷論》以諷焉，當時莫有悟者。

translations.literal: Xuan held that Liaodong could not be attacked; he composed On Pacifying the Barbarians to admonish them—in his day none understood.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed Liaodong could not be conquered; he composed On Pacifying the Barbarians to admonish the court, but at the time no one understood.

sentences.zh: 及大業之季，三征不克，炫言方驗。

translations.literal: By the end of Daye, after three campaigns failed, Xuan's words were verified.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Daye era, after three campaigns had failed, Xuan's warning was vindicated.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，牛弘引炫修律令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Niu Hong brought in Xuan to revise statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Niu Hong brought Xuan in to revise statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 高祖之世，以刀筆吏類多小人，年久長奸，勢使然也。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's reign, because clerk-scribes were mostly petty men, long years bred much wrongdoing—the force of circumstance made it so.
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's reign, because clerk-scribes were mostly petty men, long years in office bred corruption—the force of circumstance made it so.

sentences.zh: 又以風俗陵遲，婦人無節。

translations.literal: Also because customs had declined, women lacked restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Also because customs had declined and women lacked restraint.

sentences.zh: 於是立格，州縣佐史，三年而代之，九品妻無得再醮。

translations.literal: Thereupon standards were established: prefectural and county sub-clerks were replaced every three years; wives of ninth-rank officials could not remarry.
translations.idiomatic: Standards were therefore established: prefectural and county sub-clerks were replaced every three years, and wives of ninth-rank officials were forbidden to remarry.

sentences.zh: 炫著論以為不可，弘竟從之。

translations.literal: Xuan wrote an essay holding this was unacceptable; Hong in the end followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote an essay arguing the policy was wrong, but Niu Hong implemented it anyway.

sentences.zh: 諸郡置學官，及流外給廩，皆發自於炫。

translations.literal: Establishing school officers in all commanderies and providing grain rations to externally enrolled students—all originated from Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The establishment of school officers in all commanderies and the provision of grain rations to externally enrolled students both originated with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 弘嘗從容問炫曰：「案《周禮》士多而府史少，今令史百倍于前，判官減則不濟，其故何也？」

translations.literal: Hong once asked Xuan at leisure: "According to the Zhou Rites, gentlemen were many and archive clerks few; today order clerks are a hundred times those of old, yet reducing case officers would leave work undone—what is the reason?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong once asked Xuan casually: "According to the Zhou Rites, gentlemen were many and archive clerks few; today order clerks outnumber those of old a hundredfold, yet reducing case officers would leave work undone—why is this?

sentences.zh: 炫對曰：「古人委任責成，歲終考其殿最，案不重校，文不繁悉，府史之任，掌要目而已。

translations.literal: Xuan replied: "The ancients entrusted responsibility and demanded results; at year's end they examined grades of achievement; cases were not double-checked, documents were not elaborate—the task of archive clerks was merely to keep key headings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied: "The ancients entrusted responsibility and demanded results; at year's end they examined performance; cases were not double-checked and documents were not elaborate—the job of archive clerks was merely to maintain key records.

sentences.zh: 古今不同，若此之相懸也，事繁政弊，職此之由。」

translations.literal: Past and present differ; such is the gulf between them—affairs numerous and government flawed, this is the cause of the office."
translations.idiomatic: Past and present differ to this degree—government grows burdensome and corrupt because of this.

sentences.zh: 弘又問：「魏、齊之時，令史從容而已，今則不遑寧舍，其事何由？」

translations.literal: Hong asked again: "In Wei and Qi times, order clerks had leisure enough; today they have no moment's rest—what is the reason for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Hong asked again: "Under Wei and Qi, order clerks enjoyed ample leisure; today they scarcely have a moment's peace—what accounts for this?

sentences.zh: 炫對曰：「齊氏立州不過數十，三府行台，遞相統領，文書行下，不過十條。

translations.literal: Xuan replied: "The Qi established no more than several dozen provinces; the three offices and mobile regional headquarters supervised one another in succession; documents sent down numbered no more than ten items.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied: "The Qi state established only a few dozen provinces; the three central offices and mobile regional headquarters supervised one another in turn, and downward documents ran no more than ten items at a time.

sentences.zh: 今州三百，其繁一也。

translations.literal: Today there are three hundred provinces—this is the first source of the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Today there are three hundred provinces—that is the first source of the burden.

sentences.zh: 往者州唯置綱紀，郡置守丞，縣唯令而已。

translations.literal: Formerly each province set up only an inspector-general; each commandery had its prefect and assistant; each county had only a magistrate—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly each province had only an inspector-general, each commandery a prefect and assistant, and each county a magistrate and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 其所具僚，則長官自辟，受詔赴任，每州不過數十。

translations.literal: The staff they assembled were all recruited by the chief officer himself; upon receiving the summons they took up their posts—per province, no more than several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Each chief officer recruited his own staff; upon receiving an imperial summons they took up their posts—and a province had no more than a few dozen officials.

sentences.zh: 今則不然，大小之官，悉由吏部，纖介之跡，皆屬考功，其繁二也。

translations.literal: Today it is not so: offices great and small are all appointed by the Ministry of Personnel; the slightest conduct falls under the Directorate of Evaluations—this is the second source of the burden.
translations.idiomatic: Today it is otherwise: every office, high or low, is appointed by the Ministry of Personnel, and even the smallest conduct is subject to the Directorate of Evaluations—that is the second source of the burden.

sentences.zh: 省官不如省事，省事不如清心。

translations.literal: Trimming offices is not as good as trimming affairs; trimming affairs is not as good as clearing the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Reducing staff is inferior to reducing business; reducing business is inferior to clearing the mind.

sentences.zh: 官事不省而望從容，其可得乎？」

translations.literal: If official business is not reduced yet one expects leisure—can that be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: If government business is not cut back, how can one expect officials to have any leisure?

sentences.zh: 弘甚善其言而不能用。

translations.literal: Hong greatly approved his words but could not put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Hong greatly approved what Xuan said but had no power to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 納言楊達舉炫博學有文章，射策高第，除太學博士。

translations.literal: Ministerial Counsellor Yang Da recommended Xuan for broad learning and literary talent; in the placed examination he ranked among the highest and was appointed erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Ministerial Counsellor Yang Da recommended Xuan for his broad learning and literary gifts; he placed at the top of the examination field and was appointed an erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以品卑去任，還至長平，奉敕追詣行在所。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because his rank was low he left office; returning to Changping, he received an imperial order to pursue him to the emperor's traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he left office because his rank was too low; when he returned to Changping an imperial summons ordered him to proceed to the emperor's traveling residence.

sentences.zh: 或言其無行，帝遂罷之，歸於河間。

translations.literal: Some said he was without proper conduct; the emperor then dismissed him, and he returned to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused him of misconduct; the emperor dismissed him, and he returned to Hejian.

sentences.zh: 于時群盜蜂起，穀食踴貴，經籍道息，教授不行。

translations.literal: At that time bandits swarmed up everywhere; grain prices soared; the Way of the classics was stilled, and teaching ceased.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits rose everywhere like bees; grain prices soared; the Way of the classics fell silent, and instruction ceased.

sentences.zh: 炫與妻子相去百里，聲問斷絕，鬱鬱不得志，乃自為贊曰：

translations.literal: Xuan was a hundred li from his wife and children; news between them was cut off; depressed and thwarted in his aims, he composed a preface about himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was a hundred li from his wife and children; word between them was cut off; depressed and thwarted in his ambitions, he wrote a preface about himself, saying:

sentences.zh: 通人司馬相如、揚子雲、馬季長、鄭康成等，皆自敘風徽，傳芳來葉。

translations.literal: Men of discernment such as Sima Xiangru, Yang Ziyun, Ma Jichang, and Zheng Kangcheng all wrote their own accounts of elegant conduct, transmitting fragrance to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment such as Sima Xiangru, Yang Ziyun, Ma Jichang, and Zheng Kangcheng all wrote their own accounts of noble conduct, leaving their fragrance to later generations.

sentences.zh: 余豈敢仰均先達，貽笑眾昆。

translations.literal: How dare I presume to measure myself against those who came before, inviting laughter from my peers?
translations.idiomatic: How dare I presume to measure myself against those who came before and invite laughter from my peers?

sentences.zh: 待以日迫桑榆，大命將近，故友飄零，門徒雨散，溘死朝露，埋魂朔野，親故莫照其心，後人不見其跡，殆及余喘，薄言胸臆，貽及行邁，傳示州裡，使夫將來俊哲知餘鄙志耳。

translations.literal: But as the sun draws near the mulberry and elm at day's end and the great mandate approaches, old friends drift away like fallen leaves, disciples scatter like rain; one may die as suddenly as morning dew and bury one's soul in the northern wilds, with kin and friends unable to illuminate the heart and posterity unable to see one's traces—while my breath still lingers, I speak briefly from my inmost breast, leave this on my journey, and show it within the commandery, so that future worthy men may know my humble intent.
translations.idiomatic: But as the sun sinks toward the mulberry trees and my allotted span draws near, old friends drift away and disciples scatter like rain; I may die as suddenly as morning dew and leave my soul buried in the northern wilds, with kin unable to read my heart and posterity unable to see my traces—while my breath still holds, I speak briefly from my inmost breast, leave this on my journey, and show it within the commandery, so that future worthy men may know my humble intent.

sentences.zh: 餘從綰發以來，迄于白首，嬰孩為慈親所恕，棰楚未嘗加，從學為明師所矜，榎楚弗之及。

translations.literal: From the time I tied my hair as a child until white-haired age, as an infant I was indulged by a loving parent and never felt the rod; in study I was esteemed by an enlightened teacher and never reached the mulberry switch.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood until white-haired age, as an infant I was indulged by a loving parent and never felt the rod; in study I was esteemed by an enlightened teacher and never knew the mulberry switch.

sentences.zh: 暨乎敦敘邦族，交結等夷，重物輕身，先人後己。

translations.literal: And when it came to treating kinsmen with warmth, befriending equals, valuing things above self, and putting others before oneself—
translations.idiomatic: When it came to treating kinsmen with warmth, befriending equals, valuing things above self, and putting others before oneself—

sentences.zh: 昔在幼弱，樂參長者，爰及耆艾，數接後生。

translations.literal: long ago in youth I delighted in joining my elders; reaching old age, I often received the young.
translations.idiomatic: long ago in youth I delighted in the company of my elders; reaching old age, I often received the young.

sentences.zh: 學則服而不厭，誨則勞而不倦，幽情寡適，心事方違。

translations.literal: In study I never grew weary of learning; in teaching I toiled without fatigue; my hidden feelings found little satisfaction, and my heart's wishes met with constant opposition.
translations.idiomatic: In study I never grew weary of learning; in teaching I toiled without fatigue; my hidden feelings found little satisfaction, and my heart's wishes met with constant opposition.

sentences.zh: 內省生平，顧循終始，其大幸有四，其深恨有一。

translations.literal: Inwardly examining my life from beginning to end, I find four great blessings and one deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: Looking inward over my life from beginning to end, I find four great blessings and one deep regret.

sentences.zh: 性本愚蔽，家業貧窶，為父兄所饒，廁縉紳之末，遂得博覽典誥，窺涉今古，小善著於丘園，虛名聞于邦國，其幸一也。

translations.literal: My nature was originally dull and obscured, my family estate poor and wretched; indulged by father and elder brothers, I took the lowest place among the girdled and sashed and thus came to read broadly in canonical edicts and glimpse past and present; small virtues were noted in my garden retreat, empty fame was heard in the state—this is the first blessing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I was dull and my family poor; indulged by father and elder brothers, I took the lowest place among the girdled and sashed and thus came to read broadly in the classics and glimpse past and present; small virtues were noted in my garden retreat, empty fame was heard in the state—that is the first blessing.

sentences.zh: 隱顯人間，沈浮世俗，數忝徒勞之職，久執城旦之書，名不掛于白簡，事不染於丹筆，立身立行，慚恧實多，啟手啟足，庶幾可免，其幸二也。

translations.literal: Hidden and manifest in the human world, sinking and floating in worldly affairs, I repeatedly held thankless posts and long kept the convict-register books; my name was not entered on the censor's white bamboo, my deeds were not touched by the red brush; in conduct and standing I had much to blush for, yet in hands and feet I might almost escape harm—this is the second blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden and manifest in the human world, sinking and floating in worldly affairs, I repeatedly held thankless posts and long kept the convict-register books; my name never appeared on the censor's white bamboo, my deeds were never touched by the red brush; in conduct and standing I had much to blush for, yet in life and limb I might almost escape harm—that is the second blessing.

sentences.zh: 以此庸虛，屢動神眷，以此卑賤，每升天府，齊鑣驥騄，比翼鵷鴻，整緗素于鳳池，記言動於麟閣，參謁宰輔，造請群公，厚禮殊恩，增榮改價，其幸三也。

translations.literal: With such mediocrity and emptiness I repeatedly moved divine favor; with such baseness and low rank I repeatedly ascended the heavenly precincts; I matched reins with fine steeds and flew wing to wing with imperial birds; I arranged silk scrolls in the Phoenix Pool and recorded words and deeds in the Unicorn Pavilion; I attended chief ministers and called upon the great lords—rich gifts and special grace increased my honor and changed my worth—this is the third blessing.
translations.idiomatic: With such mediocrity I repeatedly moved divine favor; with such low rank I repeatedly entered the imperial precincts; I matched reins with fine steeds and flew wing to wing with imperial birds; I arranged silk scrolls in the Phoenix Pool and recorded words and deeds in the Unicorn Pavilion; I attended chief ministers and called upon the great lords—rich gifts and special grace increased my honor and changed my worth—that is the third blessing.

sentences.zh: 晝漏方盡，大耋已嗟，退反初服，歸骸故里，玩文史以怡神，閱魚鳥以散慮，觀省野物，登臨園沼，緩步代車，無罪為貴，其幸四也。

translations.literal: The day measure was nearly spent and great old age already lamented; I withdrew to my former garb and returned my bones to my native place; I enjoyed literature and history to soothe the spirit, watched fish and birds to scatter cares, observed wild things and climbed garden ponds, took slow steps in place of carriage, and held innocence dear—this is the fourth blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The day measure was nearly spent and great old age already lamented; I withdrew to my former garb and returned my bones to my native place; I enjoyed literature and history to soothe the spirit, watched fish and birds to scatter cares, observed wild things and climbed garden ponds, took slow steps in place of carriage, and held innocence dear—that is the fourth blessing.

sentences.zh: 仰休明之盛世，慨道教之陵遲，蹈先儒之逸軌，傷群言之蕪穢，馳騖墳典，厘改僻謬，修撰始畢，圖事適成，天違人願，途不我與。

translations.literal: Looking up at a glorious flourishing age, I grieved that the Way of teaching had declined; treading the abandoned tracks of earlier Confucians, I mourned the overgrown filth of many words; I raced through the tombs of the classics, corrected eccentric errors, and had just finished my editorial work when the enterprise was nearly complete—heaven opposed human wishes, and the path would not grant me passage.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up at a glorious flourishing age, I grieved that the Way of teaching had declined; treading the abandoned tracks of earlier Confucians, I mourned the overgrown filth of many words; I raced through the tombs of the classics, corrected eccentric errors, and had just finished my editorial work when the enterprise was nearly complete—heaven opposed human wishes, and the path would not grant me passage.

sentences.zh: 世路未夷，學校盡廢，道不備於當時，業不傳於身後。

translations.literal: The age's road was not yet level; schools were utterly abandoned; the Way was not perfected in its time, and the work would not be transmitted after death.
translations.idiomatic: The age's road was not yet level; schools were utterly abandoned; the Way was not perfected in its time, and the work would not be transmitted after death.

sentences.zh: 銜恨泉壤，實在茲乎？

translations.literal: To carry regret into the grave—is it not found here?
translations.idiomatic: To carry regret into the grave—is it not found here?

sentences.zh: 其深恨一也。

translations.literal: This is the one deep regret.
translations.idiomatic: That is the one deep regret.

sentences.zh: 時在郡城，糧餉斷絕，其門人多隨盜賊，哀炫窮乏，詣郡城下索炫，郡官乃出炫與之。

translations.literal: At the time he was in the commandery city; grain supplies were cut off; many of his disciples had joined the bandits; pitying Xuan's poverty and destitution, they came beneath the commandery walls to demand Xuan, and the commandery officials then released Xuan to them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was in the commandery city; grain supplies were cut off; many of his disciples had joined the bandits; pitying Xuan's poverty and destitution, they came beneath the commandery walls to demand Xuan, and the commandery officials released him to them.

sentences.zh: 炫為賊所將，過城下堡。

translations.literal: Xuan was led away by the bandits and passed the fort below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was led away by the bandits and passed the fort below the city.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊為官軍所破，炫饑餓無所依，復投縣城。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits were broken by the government army; Xuan, hungry and with nowhere to rely on, again sought refuge in the county city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits were broken by the government army; Xuan, hungry and with nowhere to turn, again sought refuge in the county city.

sentences.zh: 長吏意炫與賊相知，恐為後變，遂閉門不納。

translations.literal: The chief officer thought Xuan was acquainted with the bandits and feared future trouble, so he closed the gates and would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief officer thought Xuan was acquainted with the bandits and feared future trouble, so he closed the gates and refused to admit him.

sentences.zh: 是時夜冰寒，因此凍餒而死，時年六十八。

translations.literal: At that time the night was icy cold; because of this he died of cold and hunger; he was sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the night was icy cold; because of this he died of cold and hunger at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 其後門人諡曰宣德先生。

translations.literal: Afterward his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his disciples gave him the posthumous title Master Xuande.

sentences.zh: 炫性躁競，頗俳諧，多自矜伐，好輕侮當世，為執政所醜，由是官途不遂。

translations.literal: Xuan's nature was restless and contentious; he was quite given to jest and banter, often praised himself, and liked to slight and insult men of the age; he was detested by those in power, and hence his official career did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's nature was restless and contentious; he was quite given to jest and banter, often praised himself, and liked to slight and insult men of the age; he was detested by those in power, and hence his official career did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 著《論語述議》十卷，《春秋攻昧》十卷，《五經正名》十二卷，《孝經述議》五卷，《春秋述議》四十卷，《尚書述議》二十卷，《毛詩述議》四十卷，《注詩序》一卷，《算術》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He wrote Expositions on the Analects in ten scrolls, Attacking Obscurity in the Spring and Autumn in ten scrolls, Correct Names of the Five Classics in twelve scrolls, Expositions on the Classic of Filial Piety in five scrolls, Expositions on the Spring and Autumn in forty scrolls, Expositions on the Documents in twenty scrolls, Expositions on the Mao Odes in forty scrolls, Commentary on the Preface to the Odes in one scroll, and Arithmetic in one scroll—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Expositions on the Analects in ten scrolls, Attacking Obscurity in the Spring and Autumn in ten scrolls, Correct Names of the Five Classics in twelve scrolls, Expositions on the Classic of Filial Piety in five scrolls, Expositions on the Spring and Autumn in forty scrolls, Expositions on the Documents in twenty scrolls, Expositions on the Mao Odes in forty scrolls, Commentary on the Preface to the Odes in one scroll, and Arithmetic in one scroll—all circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 褚輝吳郡褚輝，字高明，以《三禮》學稱於江南。

translations.literal: Chu Hui—Chu Hui of Wu commandery, styled Gaoming, was famed in the lands south of the Yangzi for his study of the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Hui of Wu commandery, styled Gaoming, was famed south of the Yangzi for his study of the Three Rites.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，征天下儒術之士，悉集內史省，相次講論，輝博辯，無能屈者，由是擢為太學博士。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time, Confucian scholars were summoned from throughout the realm and all gathered in the Imperial Secretariat; they debated in succession, and Hui was so broad and eloquent that none could overcome him—hence he was promoted to erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Yang's time, Confucian scholars were summoned from throughout the realm and gathered in the Imperial Secretariat; they debated in succession, and Hui was so broad and eloquent that none could overcome him—hence he was promoted to erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 撰《禮疏》一百卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Rites Commentary in one hundred scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Rites Commentary in one hundred scrolls.

sentences.zh: 顧彪余杭顧彪，字仲文，明《尚書》、《春秋》。

translations.literal: Gu Biao—Gu Biao of Yuhang, styled Zhongwen, was expert in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Biao of Yuhang, styled Zhongwen, was expert in the Documents and the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時為秘書學士，撰《古文尚書疏》二十卷。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time he was a secretary academician and compiled Old Text Documents Commentary in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Yang's time he served as a secretary academician and compiled Old Text Documents Commentary in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 魯世達余杭魯世達，煬帝時為國子助教，撰《毛詩章句義疏》四十二卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Lu Shida—Lu Shida of Yuhang; in Emperor Yang's time he was assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy and compiled Mao Odes Chapter-and-Line Meaning Commentary in forty-two scrolls, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shida of Yuhang served as assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy under Emperor Yang and compiled Mao Odes Chapter-and-Line Meaning Commentary in forty-two scrolls, which circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 張沖吳郡張沖，字叔玄。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong—Zhang Chong of Wu commandery, styled Shuxuan.
