translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong of Wu commandery, styled Shuxuan.

sentences.zh: 仕陳為左中郎將，非其好也，乃覃思經典，撰《春秋義略》，異于杜氏七十餘事，《喪服義》三卷，《孝經義》三卷，《論語義》十卷，《前漢音義》十二卷。

translations.literal: He served Chen as Left Palace Gentleman-General—not his preference; he then pondered deeply the classics and compiled Outline of Spring and Autumn Meanings, differing from Du's school in more than seventy matters, Mourning Garments Meanings in three scrolls, Classic of Filial Piety Meanings in three scrolls, Analects Meanings in ten scrolls, and Former Han Pronunciation Meanings in twelve scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chen as left palace gentleman-general—not his preference; he then pondered deeply the classics and compiled Outline of Spring and Autumn Meanings, differing from Du's school in more than seventy matters, Mourning Garments Meanings in three scrolls, Classic of Filial Piety Meanings in three scrolls, Analects Meanings in ten scrolls, and Former Han Pronunciation Meanings in twelve scrolls.

sentences.zh: 官至漢王侍讀。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Reader to the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of reader to the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 王孝籍平原王孝籍，少好學，博覽群言，遍治五經，頗有文幹。

translations.literal: Wang Xiaoji—Wang Xiaoji of Pingyuan, from youth loved learning, read broadly in many writings, thoroughly studied the Five Classics, and had considerable literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiaoji of Pingyuan loved learning from youth, read broadly in many writings, thoroughly studied the Five Classics, and had considerable literary talent.

sentences.zh: 與河間劉炫同志友善。

translations.literal: He shared the same aims and was on friendly terms with Liu Xuan of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He shared the same aims and was on friendly terms with Liu Xuan of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，召入秘書，助王劭修國史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era he was summoned into the Imperial Library to assist Wang Shao in compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era he was summoned into the Imperial Library to assist Wang Shao in compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 劭不之禮，在省多年，而不免輸稅。

translations.literal: Shao did not treat him with courtesy; he remained in the office many years yet could not escape paying taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Shao did not treat him with courtesy; he remained in the office many years yet still had to pay taxes.

sentences.zh: 孝籍鬱鬱不得志，奏記于吏部尚書牛弘曰：

translations.literal: Xiaoji, depressed and thwarted in his aims, submitted a memorial to Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji, depressed and thwarted in his ambitions, submitted a memorial to Minister of Personnel Niu Hong, saying:

sentences.zh: 竊以毒螫寔膚，則申旦不寐，饑寒切體，亦卒歲無聊。

translations.literal: I venture to think that when poison stings truly pierce the skin, one cannot sleep from dawn to dawn; when hunger and cold cut to the flesh, one passes the year in misery as well.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to think that when poison truly stings the skin, one cannot sleep from dawn to dawn; when hunger and cold cut to the flesh, one passes the year in misery as well.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 痛苦難以安，貧窮易為蹙。

translations.literal: Pain is hard to settle into peace; poverty easily brings one to the edge.
translations.idiomatic: Pain is hard to settle into peace; poverty easily brings one to the edge.

sentences.zh: 況懷抱之內，冰火鑠脂膏，腠理之間，風霜侵骨髓，安可齰舌緘脣，吞聲飲氣，惡呻吟之響，忍酸辛之酷哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, within the breast ice and fire melt the fat and marrow; between the pores wind and frost invade the bone marrow—how can one bite the tongue and seal the lips, swallow voice and drink breath, hate the sound of groaning, and endure the bitterness of acid suffering!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the breast ice and fire melt the marrow; between the pores wind and frost invade the bones—how can one bite one's tongue and seal one's lips, swallow one's voice and choke back one's breath, hate the sound of groaning, and endure such bitter suffering!

sentences.zh: 伏惟明尚書公動哀矜之色，開寬裕之懷，咳唾足以活枯鱗，吹噓可用飛窮羽。

translations.literal: I respectfully consider that the enlightened Minister shows a countenance of pity and compassion and opens a generous breast; his cough and spittle could revive a dried fish scale, his breath and puff could lift the wings of a destitute bird.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully consider that the enlightened Minister shows a countenance of pity and compassion and opens a generous breast; his cough and spittle could revive a dried fish, his breath and puff could lift the wings of a destitute bird.

sentences.zh: 芬椒蘭之氣，暖布帛之詞，許小人之請，聞大君之聽。

translations.literal: The fragrance of pepper and orchid, warm words like cloth and silk—grant the petty man's request and let the great lord hear.
translations.idiomatic: The fragrance of pepper and orchid, warm words like cloth and silk—grant the petty man's request and let the great lord hear.

sentences.zh: 雖復山川不遠，鬼神在茲，信而有徵，言無不履，猶恐拯溺遲於援手，救經緩於扶足。

translations.literal: Even though mountains and rivers are not far and spirits and gods are present here, trust has proof and words are never unfulfilled—I still fear that saving the drowning may lag behind the outstretched hand, and rescuing the hanging man may be slower than steadying the feet.
translations.idiomatic: Even though mountains and rivers are not far and spirits and gods are present here, trust has proof and words are never unfulfilled—I still fear that saving the drowning may lag behind the outstretched hand, and rescuing the hanging man may be slower than steadying the feet.

sentences.zh: 待越人之舟楫，求魯匠之雲梯，則必懸於槁樹之枝，沒於深淵之底矣。

translations.literal: If one waits for the boat of the man of Yue or seeks the cloud ladder of the craftsman of Lu, one will surely hang from the branch of a withered tree or sink to the bottom of the deep abyss.
translations.idiomatic: If one waits for the boat of the man of Yue or seeks the cloud ladder of the craftsman of Lu, one will surely hang from the branch of a withered tree or sink to the bottom of the deep abyss.

sentences.zh: 夫以一介貧人，七年直省，課役不免，慶賞不沾，賣貢禹之田，供釋之之費，有弱子之累，乏強兄之產。

translations.literal: For a single poor man to serve seven years straight in the secretariat, unable to escape tax and corvée, untouched by rewards and honors, selling the fields of Gong Yu to pay the expenses of Shi Zhi, burdened with a weak son, lacking the estate of a strong elder brother—
translations.idiomatic: For a single poor man to serve seven years straight in the secretariat, unable to escape tax and corvée, untouched by rewards and honors, selling the fields of Gong Yu to pay the expenses of Shi Zhi, burdened with a weak son, lacking the estate of a strong elder brother—

sentences.zh: 加以老母在堂，光陰遲暮，寒暑違闕，關山超遠，齧臂為期，前途逾邈，倚閭之望，朝夕已勤。

translations.literal: add to this an old mother still at home, the light and shadow of late life, cold and heat missed in attendance, passes and mountains beyond reach, biting the arm to set a date while the road ahead grows ever more distant—the longing at the gate grows keener morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: add to this an old mother still at home, the light and shadow of late life, cold and heat missed in attendance, passes and mountains beyond reach, biting the arm to set a date while the road ahead grows ever more distant—the longing at the gate grows keener morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 謝相如之病，無官可以免，發梅福之狂，非仙所能避。

translations.literal: Like Xiangru's illness, there is no office by which to be excused; like Mei Fu's madness, not even an immortal could avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: Like Sima Xiangru's feigned illness, there is no office by which to be excused; like Mei Fu's desperate resignation, not even an immortal could avoid it.

sentences.zh: 愁疾甚乎厲鬼，人生異夫金石。

translations.literal: Grief and illness are worse than malignant ghosts; human life differs from metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Grief and illness are worse than malignant ghosts; human life is not metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 營魂且散，恐筮予無徵，齎恨入冥，則虛緣恩顧，此乃王稽所以致言，應侯為之不樂也。

translations.literal: The wandering soul is about to scatter; I fear the divination for me will show no sign; carrying regret into the dark realm, I would have relied on your grace in vain—this is why Wang Ji spoke as he did, and why Marquis Ying was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The wandering soul is about to scatter; I fear the divination for me will show no sign; carrying regret into the dark realm, I would have relied on your grace in vain—this is why Wang Ji spoke as he did, and why Marquis Ying was displeased.

sentences.zh: 潛鬢髮之內，居眉睫之間，子野未曾聞，離硃所不見，沈淪東觀，留滯南史，終無薦引，永同埋殯。

translations.literal: Hidden within hair and temples, dwelling between brow and lashes—Zi Ye never heard of it, Li Zhu never saw it; sunk in the Eastern Pavilion, detained in the Southern History, with no recommendation in the end, forever like one buried in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Hidden within hair and temples, dwelling between brow and lashes—Zi Ye never heard of it, Li Zhu never saw it; sunk in the Eastern Pavilion, detained in the Southern History, with no recommendation in the end, forever like one buried in the coffin.

sentences.zh: 三世不移，雖由寂寞，十年不調，實乏知己。

translations.literal: Three generations without transfer—though this comes from obscurity; ten years without promotion—truly because I lack a knowing patron.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations without transfer—though this comes from obscurity; ten years without promotion—truly because I lack a knowing patron.

sentences.zh: 夫不世出者，聖明之君也，不萬一者，誠賢之臣也。

translations.literal: One who does not appear in every generation is a sage and enlightened ruler; one who is not one in ten thousand is a truly worthy minister.
translations.idiomatic: One who does not appear in every generation is a sage and enlightened ruler; one who is not one in ten thousand is a truly worthy minister.

sentences.zh: 以夫不世出而逢不萬一，此小人所以為明尚書幸也。

translations.literal: That one not appearing in every generation should meet one not one in ten thousand—this is why your petty servant considers the enlightened Minister fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: That one not appearing in every generation should meet one not one in ten thousand—this is why your petty servant considers the enlightened Minister fortunate.

sentences.zh: 坐人物之源，運銓衡之柄，反披狐白，不好緇衣，此小人為明尚書不取也。

translations.literal: Sitting at the source of men and things, wielding the balance of selection, yet turning the fox-fur cloak inside out and disliking the dark robe—this your petty servant cannot approve in the enlightened Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sitting at the source of men and things, wielding the balance of selection, yet turning the fox-fur cloak inside out and disliking the dark robe—this your petty servant cannot approve in the enlightened Minister.

sentences.zh: 昔荊玉未剖，刖卞和之足，百里未用，碎禽息之首。

translations.literal: Formerly before the Jing jade was cut open, Bian He's feet were amputated; before Baili Xi was employed, Qin Xi lost his head.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly before the Jing jade was cut open, Bian He's feet were amputated; before Baili Xi was employed, Qin Xi lost his head.

sentences.zh: 居得言之地，有能用之資，增耳目之明，無手足之蹙，憚而弗為，孰知其解！

translations.literal: Occupying a place where one may speak, possessing the means to employ talent, adding clarity to eyes and ears without cramping hands and feet—if one fears and does not act, who will understand the reason!
translations.idiomatic: Occupying a place where one may speak, possessing the means to employ talent, adding clarity to eyes and ears without cramping hands and feet—if one fears and does not act, who will understand the reason!

sentences.zh: 夫官或不稱其能，士或未申其屈，一夫竊議，語流天下。

translations.literal: An office may not match one's ability; a scholar may not have his grievance heard—one man's private talk spreads through all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An office may not match one's ability; a scholar may not have his grievance heard—one man's private talk spreads through all under heaven.

sentences.zh: 勞不見圖，安能無望！

translations.literal: To toil without reward—how can one be without hope!
translations.idiomatic: To toil without reward—how can one be without hope!

sentences.zh: 儻病未及死，狂還克念，汗窮愁之簡，屬離憂之詞，記志于前修，通心於來哲，使千載之下，哀其不遇，追咎執事，有點清塵，則不肖之軀，死生為累，小人之罪，方且未刊。

translations.literal: If illness has not yet reached death and madness can still be restrained, I would sweat out words of utter despair on bamboo strips and compose verses of parting sorrow, record my intent for earlier worthies and open my heart to sages to come, so that a thousand years hence men may mourn my ill fortune and trace blame to the responsible officer, staining pure repute—then this unworthy body would be a burden in life and death, and your petty servant's fault would remain unexpunged.
translations.idiomatic: If illness has not yet reached death and madness can still be restrained, I would sweat out words of utter despair on bamboo strips and compose verses of parting sorrow, record my intent for earlier worthies and open my heart to sages to come, so that a thousand years hence men may mourn my ill fortune and trace blame to the responsible officer, staining pure repute—then this unworthy body would be a burden in life and death, and your petty servant's fault would remain unexpunged.

sentences.zh: 願少加憐湣，留心無忽！

translations.literal: I beg you to show a little pity and heed this without neglect!
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to show a little pity and heed this without neglect!

sentences.zh: 弘亦知其有學業，而竟不得調。

translations.literal: Hong also knew he had learning, yet in the end he received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Hong also knew he had learning, yet in the end he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，以教授為業，終於家。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his native place, made teaching his occupation, and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned to his native place, made teaching his occupation, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 注《尚書》及《詩》，遭亂零落。

translations.literal: His commentaries on the Documents and the Odes were scattered and lost in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His commentaries on the Documents and the Odes were scattered and lost in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古語云：「容體不足觀，勇力不足恃，族姓不足道，先祖不足稱，然而顯聞四方，流聲後胤者，其唯學乎？」

translations.literal: The historiographer says: An old saying runs: "Physique is not worth looking at, courage and strength are not worth relying on, clan name is not worth speaking of, forebears are not worth praising—yet what makes one renowned in the four directions and leaves a name to posterity? Is it not learning?"
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: An old saying runs: "Physique is not worth looking at, courage and strength are not worth relying on, clan name is not worth speaking of, forebears are not worth praising—yet what makes one renowned in the four directions and leaves a name to posterity? Is it not learning?"

sentences.zh: 信哉斯言也。

translations.literal: How true these words are.
translations.idiomatic: How true these words are.

sentences.zh: 暉遠、榮伯之徒，篤志不倦，自求諸己，遂能聞道下風，稱珍席上。

translations.literal: Men such as Huiyuan and Rongbo, with steadfast resolve never weary, seeking within themselves, were able to hear the Way from below and be called treasures at the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Huiyuan and Rongbo, with steadfast resolve never weary, seeking within themselves, were able to hear the Way from below and be called treasures at the mat.

sentences.zh: 或聚徒千百，或服冕乘軒，見重明時，實惟稽古之力也。

translations.literal: Some gathered disciples by the hundreds and thousands; some wore caps and rode chariots; honored in enlightened times—these were truly the power of revering antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Some gathered disciples by the hundreds and thousands; some wore caps and rode chariots; honored in enlightened times—these were truly the power of revering antiquity.

sentences.zh: 江陽從容雅望，風韻閑遠，清談高論，籍甚當年；

translations.literal: Jiangyang had an easy bearing and elegant reputation, a manner leisurely and far-reaching, pure talk and lofty discourse—greatly famed in his day;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyang had an easy bearing and elegant reputation, a manner leisurely and far-reaching, pure talk and lofty discourse—greatly famed in his day;

sentences.zh: 彥之敦經悅史，砥身礪行，志存典制，動蹈規矩；

translations.literal: Yanzhi loved the classics and delighted in history, honed body and sharpened conduct, kept ritual institutions in mind, and in action followed the rule;
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi loved the classics and delighted in history, honed body and sharpened conduct, kept ritual institutions in mind, and in action followed the rule;

sentences.zh: 何妥通涉俊爽，神情警悟，雅有口才，兼擅詞筆，然訐以為直，失儒者之風焉；

translations.literal: He Tuo was broadly versed and brilliantly alert, spiritually keen and quick to understand, elegantly gifted in speech, and also skilled with pen and phrase—yet he took denunciation for uprightness and lost the manner of the Confucian;
translations.idiomatic: He Tuo was broadly versed and brilliantly alert, spiritually keen and quick to understand, elegantly gifted in speech, and also skilled with pen and phrase—yet he took denunciation for uprightness and lost the manner of the Confucian;

sentences.zh: 劉焯道冠縉紳，數窮天象，既精且博，洞幽究微，銘深致遠，源流不測，數百年來，斯人而已；

translations.literal: Liu Chuo's Way topped the girdled and sashed; he exhausted the numbers of heaven's signs—both precise and broad, penetrating the hidden and probing the subtle, inscribing the deep and reaching far, his source and flow unfathomable; in several hundred years, this man alone;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chuo's Way topped the girdled and sashed; he exhausted the numbers of heaven's signs—both precise and broad, penetrating the hidden and probing the subtle, inscribing the deep and reaching far, his source and flow unfathomable; in several hundred years, this man alone;

sentences.zh: 劉炫學實通儒，才堪成務，九流七略，無不該覽，雖探賾索隱，不逮於焯，裁成義說，文雅過之。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan's learning was truly that of a comprehensive Confucian; his talent could fulfill affairs; of the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries there was none he did not cover—though in probing the hidden and seeking the obscure he did not reach Chuo, in framing meanings and composing explications his literary elegance surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan's learning was truly that of a comprehensive Confucian; his talent could fulfill affairs; of the Nine Schools and Seven Summaries there was none he did not cover—though in probing the hidden and seeking the obscure he did not reach Chuo, in framing meanings and composing explications his literary elegance surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 並道亞生知，時不我與，或才登于下士，或餒棄於溝壑，惜矣。

translations.literal: Both men's Way approached innate knowledge, yet the age did not grant them time; one reached only the lowest rank of scholar, one was abandoned starving in a ditch—alas.
translations.idiomatic: Both men's Way approached innate knowledge, yet the age did not grant them time; one reached only the lowest rank of scholar, one was abandoned starving in a ditch—alas.

sentences.zh: 子夏有言：「死生有命，富貴在天。」

translations.literal: Zixia said: "Life and death are a matter of fate; wealth and rank are in heaven's hands."
translations.idiomatic: Zixia said: "Life and death are a matter of fate; wealth and rank are in heaven's hands."

sentences.zh: 天之所與者聰明，所不與者貴仕，上聖且猶不免，焯、炫其如命何！

translations.literal: What heaven grants is intelligence; what it does not grant is noble office—even the highest sage could not escape this; what could Chuo and Xuan do against fate!
translations.idiomatic: What heaven grants is intelligence; what it does not grant is noble office—even the highest sage could not escape this; what could Chuo and Xuan do against fate!
